newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE RUBBER DULL, TRADE MULLS INDONESIAN NEWS.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE RUBBER DULL, TRADE MULLS INDONESIAN NEWS.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was quiet by midday on Thursday with the trade digesting news that Bank Indonesia has scrapped announcing its intervention and conversion bands on the rupiah, dealers said.

"It may have an effect later, but we'd like to see how the Indonesian trade reacts first. The local exchange was almost untraded this morning, so its a little too early to say what kind of impact it may have on the market," a dealer said.
Traders said the managed float of the rupiah may help Indonesian rubber producers, but this is offset by weak demand due to the holiday season in the U.S., Europe and Japan.
The rubber trade was also waiting later on Thursday for direction from Japan and the major rubber consumers like Bridgestone, which is said to have bought some TSR20 rubber yesterday.
"We're hoping for some buying to emerge again today from the big boys," one trader said. "But the currency problems in the region has made doing business a bit difficult."
At around 0445 GMT, September TSR20 was indicated at 93.00-95.00 U.S. cents a kg from 95.00 cents.
